new_facts.fact: Cornell's stated reasons for the two-year requirement
new_facts.value: Students who live on campus show increased academic achievement, improved social-emotional adjustment and a stronger ability to build community; the meal plan ensures proper nutrition and guards against food insecurity, which has increased at colleges nationwide
new_facts.source_title: Residential Policy, Cornell Student & Campus Life

new_facts.value: First- and second-years must live on campus or in approved affiliated housing through the spring semester of their second academic year; juniors and seniors are not guaranteed on-campus housing
new_facts.source_title: Current Undergraduate Application Process, Cornell Student & Campus Life

new_facts.value: Failure to indicate intent to live in a sorority, fraternity, co-op or affiliated house by March 15 results in completing the requirement in on-campus housing
new_facts.source_title: Spring Housing Selection for Rising Sophomores, Cornell Student & Campus Life

new_facts.fact: Student reaction to the sophomore rule
new_facts.value: Chad Rubin '25 said the rule limits independence; Ashley Jian '24 lives off campus partly to cook and avoid the West Campus House Meal Plan (Jian, not Rubin or Lilienfeld, made the cooking point)
new_facts.source_title: As Cornell Requires University Housing for Sophomores, Students Weigh Options, The Cornell Daily Sun
